why: Works listed on the artist's site, several marked open for participation; Receipt was acquired by Fingerprints DAO in 2024 and Still Remember was a 2024 Lumen Prize finalist. Not yet researched.

name: James Bloom, other networked works (Transactional space, Unseen changes)
why: His bio says his software works often connect hundreds of participants online; the projects listed on his site besides GOLD were not checked.

name: Ed Fornieles, Animal House (Guest Projects, London, 2011)
why: College-party performances for which, by the artist's account in Rhizome (2012), over 200 people were briefed in advance on characters and actions taken from films, pranks and college scenarios. Passes the test on paper; needs images or video.

name: Christian Falsnaes, Influence (2012)
why: Performance in which the audience become extras in a music video, described in the Berlinische Galerie's 2017 handout; check the artist's page for media and the rules given to the audience.

name: Jonas Lund, Network Maintenance (2025)
why: For the network/social batch (not on a blockchain). Limited edition of networked wall devices; terms of ownership require each owner to keep the device online and interact with it, neglect shows as decay on the device and across the whole network, which goes dormant if too few nodes stay active. Shown with Office Impart at Zero 10, Art Basel Hong Kong (March 2026) and Tokyo Jazz Club (1–8 November 2026). Verified images: https://network-maintenance.com/images/device/OfficeImpart_JonasLund_MBP-3.jpg , https://network-maintenance.com/images/screenshots/01.jpg

Not in the gallery; check whether collectors' reveals count as group behaviour.

name: Brigitta Muntendorf, Last Show (CONNECT – The Audience as Artist, 2026)
why: Commission by Ensemble Modern, London Sinfonietta, Het Muziek, Remix Ensemble and Ensemble intercontemporain: listeners answer questions about their affiliations and roles through a smartphone voting tool while the music plays, results shown live and comparable across cities. World premiere announced for 17 October 2026 at Donaueschinger Musiktage (Amsterdam on 3 December 2026); only the pre-premiere interview could be opened, so a review or documentation is needed before adding.

name: Keith Yamashita, What Season Is It, America? (Brooklyn Museum, 21–25 October 2026)
why: Visitors pick one of nearly 500 printed poems and photographs from a circle on the floor, bring it to a rotating 12-seat table and answer 'Why did you bring this?'; a hanko stamp closes each sitting. Passes the test on paper, but the only opened source is a Cool Hunting preview of 13 October 2026 and another outlet describes a lobby banner display; confirm with the museum's page that it ran as described.

name: Yayoi Kusama, The Obliteration Room (2002–)
